title: Measuring the Seat Days of an Additional Driver on a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan Election
content:
The seat days are the days of the trip the additional driver's fee is measured across on a Keyturn Guest
Protection Plan election. Three conventions meter them, and which one applies turns on whether the trip has
already begun and on how many days of cover the election carries.

**Where the additional driver is taken on once the trip has begun and the election covers 30 days or more**,
the seat days are the whole weeks of the trip still to run, counted from the day the driver is taken on and
rounded up to a whole week, each week counted as seven days.

**Where the additional driver is taken on once the trip has begun and the election covers fewer than 30 days**,
the seat days are the calendar days of the trip still to run, counted from the day the driver is taken on, that
day included.

**Where the additional driver is taken on before the trip has begun**, the seat days are the whole of the
election's covered days.

The fee for the additional driver is measured across the seat days out of the election's covered days, so what
is taken is the level's additional driver fee in the proportion the seat days bear to the covered days.

## The three conventions side by side

| Has the trip begun? | Days of cover the election carries | How the seat days are counted |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 30 or more | Whole weeks still to run from the day the driver is taken on, part week counted as a whole week, each week seven days |
| Yes | Fewer than 30 | Calendar days still to run from the day the driver is taken on, that day included |
| No | Any number | The whole of the election's covered days |

## Worked on hypothetical trips

**A long trip already running.** An election carrying 45 days of cover, on a trip whose last reserved day is 10
days after the day the driver is taken on, has 11 calendar days still to run counting the day the driver is
taken on. Eleven days is one whole week and a part week, so two weeks are counted, and the seat days are 14.

**A short trip already running.** An election carrying 6 days of cover, on a trip whose last reserved day is 2
days after the day the driver is taken on, has 3 calendar days still to run counting that day, and the seat days
are 3.

**Either trip before it begins.** Taken on before the trip has begun, the first election gives seat days of 45
and the second gives 6, being in each case the whole of the election's covered days.

**On the threshold.** An election carrying exactly 30 days of cover on a trip already running takes the whole-week
convention; one carrying 29 takes the calendar-day convention.
